metadata_sample.rules_text:
- If sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices — correct by reducing forecast slope or adding downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at recent high minus 5–10%.
- When sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., >0.2), model frequently overreacts — dampen forecast growth rate or introduce sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a peak, model often fails to recognize it — adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- In low-sentiment environments, model tends to forecast flat or upward trends — force downward bias if true price drops >10% from recent peak.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early divergence downward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence in trend.
